harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 with inventory-worker running as the dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc account. The service is confined to a root-owned chroot; only /var/lib/inventory is writable. It remained healthy and confined after a verified node reboot, with the OS release and kernel unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the system account inventorysvc with UID/GID 992 and a nologin shell.
Created the root-owned /srv/inventory-chroot and a minimal runtime using existing OS components.
Created /var/lib/inventory owned by inventorysvc with mode 0750 and bind-mounted it into the chroot.
Installed, enabled, and started inventory-worker.service with RootDirectory, ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, and an empty capability set.
Verified namespace confinement using successful and denied write probes.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified changed boot identity, persisted data, service recovery, and continued heartbeats.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc account and managed inventory-worker service
evidence.summary: Shows inventorysvc as UID/GID 992, inventory-worker active and enabled with User/Group=inventorysvc, and successful recovery after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Root-owned chroot with /var/lib/inventory as the only writable application directory
evidence.summary: Shows the chroot owned by root, the data directory owned by inventorysvc, and live pre/post-reboot namespace tests where /var/lib/inventory is writable while / and /usr/local/bin are read-only and host /etc is hidden.

evidence.requirement: Background worker health and persistent application data
evidence.summary: Heartbeat counts increase before and after reboot; prior data persists and the worker resumes with a new PID.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both observations show RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Captures healthy baseline and boot ID 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d, acknowledged delayed reboot, changed boot ID b76ac024-c677-4186-959d-249805284728, and direct post-restart service/data recovery.
